Main.sentence: Super Bowl XX was an ___E:American football U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football)___ game between the ___E:National Football Conference U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_Conference)___ (NFC) champion ___E:Chicago Bears U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_Chicago_Bears_season)___ and the ___E:American Football Conference U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Football_Conference)___ (AFC) champion ___E:New England Patriots U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_New_England_Patriots_season)___ to decide the ___E:National Football League U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League)___ (NFL) champion for the ___E:1985 season U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_NFL_season)___ .

The Bears defeated the Patriots by the score of 46–10, capturing their first NFL championship since ___E:1963 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1963_NFL_Championship_Game)___ , three years prior to the birth of the Super Bowl. Super Bowl XX was played on January 26, 1986, at the ___E:Louisiana Superdome U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_Superdome)___ in ___E:New Orleans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans)___ .

This was the fourth Super Bowl and, to date, the last time in which both teams made their Super Bowl debuts. [a] The Bears entered the game after becoming the second team in NFL history to win 15 regular season games.

With their then-revolutionary ___E:46 defense U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/46_defense)___ , Chicago led the league in several defensive categories, outscored their opponents with a staggering margin of 456–198, and recorded two postseason shutouts.

The Patriots were considered a ___E:Cinderella team U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinderella_(sports))___ during the 1985 season, and posted an 11–5 regular season record, but entered the playoffs as a ___E:wild card U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild_card_(sports))___ because of ___E:tiebreakers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiebreaker)___ ; defying the odds, New England posted three road playoff wins to advance to Super Bowl XX.
In their victory over the Patriots, the Bears set or tied Super Bowl records for sacks (seven), fewest rushing yards allowed (seven), and margin of victory (36 points).

At the time, New England broke the record for the quickest lead in Super Bowl history, with ___E:Tony Franklin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Franklin_(kicker))___ 's 36-yard field goal 1:19 into the first quarter after a Chicago fumble.

But the Patriots were eventually held to negative yardage (−19) throughout the entire first half, and finished with just 123 total yards from scrimmage, the second lowest total yards in Super Bowl history, behind the ___E:Minnesota Vikings U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Vikings)___ (119 total yards) in ___E:Super Bowl IX U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_IX)___ .

Bears defensive end ___E:Richard Dent U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Dent)___ , who had 1.5 quarterback sacks, forced two fumbles, and blocked a pass, was named the game's ___E:Most Valuable Player U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_Most_Valuable_Player_Award)___ (MVP).

Although he posted relatively mediocre game statistics and failed to score a touchdown himself, star running back ___E:Walter Payton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Payton)___ was also later credited as being a major factor in the Bears' victory on account of the Patriots' heavy coverage of him giving other members of the team more and better opportunities to score.
The telecast of the game on ___E:NBC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_on_NBC)___ was watched by an estimated 92.57 million viewers.
To commemorate the 20th Super Bowl, all previous Super Bowl MVPs were honored during the pregame ceremonies.

NFL owners voted to award Super Bowl XX to ___E:New Orleans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans)___ on December 14, 1982, at the owners' mid-season meeting held in ___E:Dallas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas)___ .

This would be the sixth time that New Orleans hosted the Super Bowl. ___E:Tulane Stadium U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulane_Stadium)___ was the site of ___E:IV U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_IV)___ , ___E:VI U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_VI)___ , and ___E:IX U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_IX)___ ; while the ___E:Louisiana Superdome U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caesars_Superdome)___ previously hosted ___E:XII U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XII)___ and ___E:XV U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XV)___ .

Hosts for both ___E:XIX U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XIX)___ and XX would be selected, and potentially ___E:XXI U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXI)___ as well. A total of ten cities put in bids: ___E:Palo Alto U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palo_Alto,_California)___ ( ___E:Stanford Stadium U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanford_Stadium)___ ), ___E:New Orleans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans)___ ( ___E:Superdome U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caesars_Superdome)___ ), ___E:Miami U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami)___ ( ___E:Orange Bowl U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Orange_Bowl)___ ), ___E:Houston U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston)___ ( ___E:Rice Stadium U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rice_Stadium_(Rice_University))___ ), ___E:Seattle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle)___ ( ___E:Kingdome U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdome)___ ), ___E:Detroit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit)___ ( ___E:Silverdome U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pontiac_Silverdome)___ ), ___E:Pasadena U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pasadena,_California)___ ( ___E:Rose Bowl U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rose_Bowl_(stadium))___ ), ___E:Tampa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa)___ ( ___E:Tampa Stadium U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa_Stadium)___ ), ___E:Anaheim U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anaheim,_California)___ ( ___E:Anaheim Stadium U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angel_Stadium)___ ), and ___E:Jacksonville U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacksonville,_Florida)___ ( ___E:Gator Bowl U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gator_Bowl_Stadium)___ ).

As part of their pitch, the representatives from New Orleans stressed that if they were not selected for XX, due to scheduling conflicts, they would not be able to host the Super Bowl again until 1990. ___E:Stanford Stadium U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanford_Stadium)___ was picked for ___E:XIX U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XIX)___ ,  and ___E:Rice Stadium U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rice_Stadium_(Rice_University))___ was speculated for XXI, but ultimately no decision was made for that game. Yet again, Miami was rejected, due to the aging condition of the ___E:Orange Bowl U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Orange_Bowl)___ .
A proposed sales tax levy to pay for a new stadium had failed at the ballot box on November 2, further sinking any chances for ___E:South Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Florida)___ .

Under head coach ___E:Mike Ditka U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Ditka)___ , who won the 1985 ___E:NFL Coach of the Year Award U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Coach_of_the_Year_Award)___ , the Bears went 15–1 in the regular season, becoming the second NFL team to win 15 regular season games, while outscoring their opponents with a staggering margin of 456–198.

The Bears' defense, the " ___E:46 defense U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/46_defense)___ ", allowed the fewest points (198), fewest total yards (4,135), and fewest rushing yards of any team during the regular season (1,319).
They also led the league in interceptions (34) and ranked third in sacks (64).

___E:Pro Bowl U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_Bowl)___ quarterback ___E:Jim McMahon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_McMahon)___ (who had the best season of his career) provided the team with a solid passing attack, throwing for 2,392 yards and 15 touchdowns (both career highs), while also rushing for 252 yards and three touchdowns.
Running back ___E:Walter Payton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Payton)___ , who was then the NFL's all-time leading rusher with 14,860 yards, rushed for 1,551 yards.
He also caught 49 passes for 500 yards, and scored 11 touchdowns.

Linebacker ___E:Mike Singletary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Singletary)___ won the ___E:NFL Defensive Player of the Year Award U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Defensive_Player_of_the_Year_Award)___ by recording three sacks, three fumble recoveries, and one interception.

One of the most distinguishable players on defense was rookie lineman ___E:William "The Refrigerator" Perry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Perry_(American_football))___ , who came into training camp before the season weighing over 380 pounds.

However, after Bears defensive coordinator ___E:Buddy Ryan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddy_Ryan)___ told the press that the team "wasted" their first round draft pick on him, Perry lost some weight and ended up being an effective defensive tackle, finishing the season with five sacks.

He got even more attention when Ditka started putting him in the game at the fullback position during offensive plays near the opponent's goal line. During the regular season, Perry rushed for two touchdowns, caught a pass for another touchdown, and was frequently a lead blocker for Payton during goal line plays.
In addition to Singletary and Perry, the starting 11 in the Bears' "46 defense" were all impact players.

The defensive line featured three future ___E:Hall of Famers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_Football_Hall_of_Fame)___ : defensive end ___E:Richard Dent U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Dent)___ led the NFL in sacks (17), while tackle/end ___E:Dan Hampton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Hampton)___ recorded 6.5 sacks, and tackle ___E:Steve McMichael U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_McMichael)___ compiled eight.

Outside linebacker ___E:Otis Wilson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otis_Wilson)___ had 10.5 sacks and three interceptions, with fellow outside linebacker ___E:Wilber Marshall U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilber_Marshall)___ adding six sacks and four interceptions.

In the secondary, cornerback ___E:Leslie Frazier U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leslie_Frazier)___ (who would suffer a career-ending knee injury in the game) had six interceptions, cornerback ___E:Mike Richardson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Richardson_(American_football,_born_1961))___ recorded four interceptions, strong safety ___E:Dave Duerson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Duerson)___ had five interceptions, and free safety ___E:Gary Fencik U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Fencik)___ contributed five interceptions and a team-high 118 tackles.

Chicago's main offensive weapon was Payton and the running game. A big reason for Payton's success was fullback ___E:Matt Suhey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Suhey)___ as the primary lead blocker.
Suhey was also a good ball carrier, rushing for 471 yards and catching 33 passes for 295 yards.

The team's rushing was also aided by Pro Bowlers ___E:Jim Covert U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Covert)___ and ___E:Jay Hilgenberg U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Hilgenberg)___ and the rest of the Bears' offensive line including Mark Bortz, Keith Van Horne, and Tom Thayer.

In their passing game, the Bears' primary deep threat was wide receiver ___E:Willie Gault U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Gault)___ , who caught 33 passes for 704 yards, an average of 21.3 yards per catch, and returned 22 kickoffs for 557 yards and a touchdown.
Tight end ___E:Emery Moorehead U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emery_Moorehead)___ was another key contributor, catching 35 passes for 481 yards.
Wide receiver ___E:Dennis McKinnon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dennis_McKinnon)___ was another passing weapon, recording 31 receptions, 555 yards, and seven touchdowns.

On special teams, ___E:Kevin Butler U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Butler_(American_football))___ set a rookie scoring record with 144 points, making 31 of 37 field goals (83%) and 51 of 51 extra points.

Meanwhile, the players brought their characterizations to the national stage with " ___E:The Super Bowl Shuffle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Super_Bowl_Shuffle)___ ", a ___E:rap U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip_hop_music)___ song the Bears recorded for which they filmed a ___E:music video U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video)___ during the 1985 season.

Although it was in essence a novelty song, it peaked at number 41 on the Billboard charts and even received a ___E:Grammy Award U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award)___ nomination for ___E:Best R&B Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_R%26B_Performance_by_a_Duo_or_Group_with_Vocals)___ in ___E:1987 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/29th_Grammy_Awards)___ .

The Patriots were a ___E:Cinderella team U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinderella_(sports))___ during the 1985 season because many sports writers and fans thought they were lucky to make the playoffs at all. New England began the season losing three of their first five games, but won six consecutive games to finish with an 11–5 record.

However, the 11–5 mark only earned them third place in the ___E:AFC East U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_East)___ behind the ___E:Miami Dolphins U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Dolphins)___ and the ___E:New York Jets U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Jets)___ .

Quarterback ___E:Tony Eason U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Eason)___ , in his third year in the NFL, was inconsistent during the regular season, completing 168 out of 299 passes for 2,156 yards and 11 touchdowns, but also 17 interceptions.
His backup, ___E:Steve Grogan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Grogan)___ , was considered one of the best reserve quarterbacks in the league.
Grogan was the starter in six of the Patriots' games, and finished the regular season with 85 out of 156 completions for 1,311 yards, 7 touchdowns, and 5 interceptions.
Wide receiver ___E:Stanley Morgan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Morgan)___ provided the team with a good deep threat, catching 39 passes for 760 yards and 5 touchdowns.

On the other side of the field, multi-talented wide receiver ___E:Irving Fryar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irving_Fryar)___ was equally effective, catching 39 passes for 670 yards, while also rushing for 27 yards, gaining another 559 yards returning punts and kickoffs, and scoring 10 touchdowns.
But like the Bears, the Patriots' main strength on offense was their rushing attack.
Halfback ___E:Craig James U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craig_James_(running_back))___ rushed for 1,227 yards, caught 27 passes for 370 yards, and scored 7 touchdowns.
Fullback ___E:Tony Collins U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Collins_(American_football))___ rushed for 657 yards, recorded a team-leading 52 receptions for 549 yards, and scored 5 touchdowns.

The Patriots also had an outstanding offensive line, led by Pro Bowl tackle ___E:Brian Holloway U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Holloway)___ and future Hall of Fame guard ___E:John Hannah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hannah_(American_football))___ .
New England's defense ranked 5th in the league in fewest yards allowed (5,048).
Pro Bowl linebacker ___E:Andre Tippett U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andre_Tippett)___ led the AFC with 16.5 sacks and recovered 3 fumbles.
Pro Bowl linebacker ___E:Steve Nelson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Nelson_(American_football))___ was also a big defensive weapon, excelling at pass coverage and run stopping.
Also, the Patriots' secondary only gave up 14 touchdown passes during the season, second fewest in the league.

Pro Bowl defensive back ___E:Raymond Clayborn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_Clayborn)___ recorded 6 interceptions for 80 return yards and 1 touchdown, while Pro Bowler ___E:Fred Marion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_Marion)___ had 7 interceptions for 189 return yards.
In the playoffs, the Patriots qualified as the AFC's second ___E:wild card U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild_card_(sports))___ .

But the Patriots, under head coach Raymond Berry, defied the odds, beating the ___E:New York Jets U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Jets)___ 26–14, ___E:Los Angeles Raiders U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Raiders)___ 27–20, and the Dolphins 31–14 – all on the road – to make it to the Super Bowl.    The win against Miami had been especially surprising, not only because Miami was the only team to beat Chicago in the season, but also because New England had not won in the Orange Bowl (Miami's then-home field) since 1966, the Dolphins' first season (then in the ___E:AFL U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Football_League)___ ).
The Patriots had lost to Miami there 18 consecutive times, including a 30–27 loss in their 15th game of the season.

But New England dominated the Dolphins in the AFC Championship Game, recording two interceptions from quarterback ___E:Dan Marino U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Marino)___ and recovering 4 fumbles.
New England remains the only team to finish third in their division and qualify for the Super Bowl in the same season.

Meanwhile, the Bears became the first and only team in NFL history to shut out both of their opponents in the playoffs, beating the ___E:New York Giants U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Giants)___ 21–0 and the ___E:Los Angeles Rams U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Rams)___ 24–0.
Much of the Super Bowl pregame hype centered on Bears quarterback ___E:Jim McMahon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_McMahon)___ .
First, he was fined by the NFL during the playoffs for a violation of the league's dress code, wearing a head band from ___E:Adidas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adidas)___ .
He then started to wear a head band where he hand-wrote "Rozelle", after then-league commissioner ___E:Pete Rozelle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_Rozelle)___ .

McMahon suffered a strained ___E:glute U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glute)___ as the result of a hit taken in the NFC Championship Game and flew his acupuncturist into New Orleans to get treatment.
During practice four days before the Super Bowl, he wore a headband reading "Acupuncture".
During a Bears practice before the Super Bowl, McMahon ___E:mooned U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mooning)___ a helicopter that was hovering over the practice.

Another anecdote involving McMahon during the Super Bowl anticipation involved ___E:WDSU U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WDSU-TV)___ sports anchor ___E:Buddy Diliberto U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddy_Diliberto)___ reporting a quote attributed to McMahon, where he had allegedly referred to the women of New Orleans as " ___E:sluts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slut)___ " on a local morning sports talk show. This caused wide controversy among the women of New Orleans and McMahon began receiving calls from irate fans in his hotel.

A groggy McMahon, who had not been able to sleep well because of all the calls he had gotten, was confronted by Mike Ditka later that morning and denied making the statement, saying he would not have even been awake to make the comment when he was said to have done so. He was supported in his claim by WLS reporter Les Grobstein, who was present when the alleged statements were made.  WDSU would later retract the statement, have an on-air apology read by the station's general manager during the noon newscast on January 23, and suspend Diliberto.

As the ___E:designated home team U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl#Home_team_designation)___ in the annual rotation between AFC and NFC teams, the Patriots wore their red jerseys with white pants, even though they wore white jerseys with red pants for all home games during the regular season.
New England made the switch for the Super Bowl after winning vs. the Jets and Dolphins wearing red jerseys.
The Bears donned their road white uniforms with navy pants.

The game was broadcast in the United States by ___E:NBC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_on_NBC)___ , with ___E:play-by-play announcer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Play-by-play)___ ___E:Dick Enberg U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Enberg)___ , and ___E:color commentators U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Color_commentator)___ ___E:Merlin Olsen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merlin_Olsen)___ and ___E:Bob Griese U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Griese)___ .

Griese worked in a separate booth from Enberg and Olsen.  ___E:Bob Costas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Costas)___ and his NFL '85 castmates, ___E:Ahmad Rashad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmad_Rashad)___ and ___E:Pete Axthelm U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_Axthelm)___ anchored the pregame, halftime and postgame coverage.

Other contributors included ___E:Charlie Jones U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_Jones_(sportscaster))___ (recapping ___E:Super Bowl I U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_I)___ ), ___E:Larry King U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_King)___ (interviewing ___E:Mike Ditka U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Ditka)___ and ___E:Raymond Berry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_Berry)___ ), and ___E:Bill Macatee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Macatee)___ (profiling Patriots owner ___E:Billy Sullivan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Sullivan_(American_football))___ and his family).

The pregame coverage also included a skit featuring comedian ___E:Rodney Dangerfield U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodney_Dangerfield)___ , an interview by NBC Nightly News anchor ___E:Tom Brokaw U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Brokaw)___ of ___E:United States President U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ ___E:Ronald Reagan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan)___ at the ___E:White House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House)___ (this would not become a regular Super Bowl pregame feature until ___E:Super Bowl XLIII U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLIII)___ , when Today show host ___E:Matt Lauer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Lauer)___ interviewed U.S.

President ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ ) and a concept devised by then-NBC Sports executive ___E:Michael Weisman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Weisman)___ which became known as the "Silent Minute,"  a one-minute countdown featuring a black screen with a ___E:digital clock U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_clock)___ which morphed into ___E:Roman numerals U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_numerals)___ when it reached twenty seconds remaining and accompanied by ___E:Leroy Anderson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leroy_Anderson)___ 's " ___E:The Syncopated Clock U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Syncopated_Clock)___ ."

The national radio broadcast was aired by ___E:NBC Radio U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_on_NBC_Radio)___ , which outbid CBS Radio for the nationwide NFL contract in March 1985. ___E:Don Criqui U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Criqui)___ was the play-by-play announcer, with ___E:Bob Trumpy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Trumpy)___ as the color analyst. ___E:WGN-AM U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WGN-AM)___ carried the game in the Chicago area (and thanks to WGN's 50,000-watt clear-channel signal, to much of the continental United States), with ___E:Wayne Larrivee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_Larrivee)___ on play-by-play, and ___E:Jim Hart U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Hart_(American_football))___ and ___E:Dick Butkus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Butkus)___ providing commentary. ___E:WEEI U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WEZE)___ carried the game in the Boston area, with ___E:John Carlson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carlson_(sportscaster))___ and ___E:Jon Morris U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Morris)___ on the call.

NBC's broadcast garnered the third highest ___E:Nielsen rating U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nielsen_rating)___ of any Super Bowl to date at 48.3, but it ended up being the first Super Bowl to garner over 90 million viewers, the highest ever at that time.

The series premiere of The Last Precinct was ___E:NBC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC)___ 's ___E:Super Bowl lead-out program U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Super_Bowl_lead-out_programs)___ .

Super Bowl XX was simulcast in Canada on ___E:CTV U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CTV_Television_Network)___ and broadcast on ___E:Channel 4 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channel_4)___ in the United Kingdom. ___E:Canal 5 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_5_(Mexico))___ also had the game in Mexico, with ___E:play-by-play announcers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Play-by-play)___ ___E:Toño de Valdés U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=To%C3%B1o_de_Vald%C3%A9s&action=edit&redlink=1)___ , ___E:Enrique Burak U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Enrique_Burak&action=edit&redlink=1)___ and ___E:color commentator U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Color_commentator)___ ___E:Pepe Segarra U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pepe_Segarra&action=edit&redlink=1)___ .
This was the first Super Bowl that this long lasting trio ever called together.
Super Bowl XX is featured on NFL's Greatest Games under the title Super Bears with narration by ___E:Don LaFontaine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_LaFontaine)___ .
This was the first year that the NFL itself implemented the pregame entertainment.

The pregame entertainment show began after the players left the field and ended with kick-off. Lesslee Fitzmorris created and directed the show. To celebrate the 20th Super Bowl game, the Most Valuable Players of the previous Super Bowls were featured during the pregame festivities.
The number one song of the year coupled with video plays from each Super Bowl accompanied the presentation of each player.
Performers formed the score of each championship game. The show concluded with the question of who would be the next Super Bowl Champions.

This would start a tradition occurring every ten years (in Super Bowls ___E:XXX U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXX)___ , ___E:XL U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XL)___ and ___E:50 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_50)___ ) in which past Super Bowl MVPs would be honored before the game.

After ___E:trumpeter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trumpet)___ ___E:Wynton Marsalis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wynton_Marsalis)___ performed the national anthem, ___E:Bart Starr U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bart_Starr)___ , MVP of ___E:Super Bowl I U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_I)___ and ___E:Super Bowl II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_II)___ , ___E:tossed the coin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coin_flipping)___ .
The performance event group ___E:Up with People U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Up_with_People)___ performed during the halftime show titled "Beat of the Future".
Up with People dancers portrayed various scenes into the future.

This was the last Super Bowl to feature Up with People as a halftime show, though they later performed in the ___E:Super Bowl XXV U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXV)___ pregame show. The halftime show was dedicated to the memory of Dr. ___E:Martin Luther King Jr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Luther_King_Jr.)___ (the first observance of ___E:Martin Luther King Jr. Day U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Luther_King_Jr._Day)___ had been held the previous Monday).

The Patriots took the then-quickest lead in Super Bowl history after linebacker ___E:Larry McGrew U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_McGrew)___ recovered a fumble by running back ___E:Walter Payton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Payton)___ at the Bears 19-yard line on the second play of the game  (the Bears themselves would break this record in ___E:Super Bowl XLI U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLI)___ when ___E:Devin Hester U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Hester)___ ran back the opening kickoff for a touchdown).

Bears quarterback ___E:Jim McMahon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_McMahon)___ took responsibility for this fumble after the game, saying he had called the wrong play which left Payton alone with no blockers.

This set up kicker ___E:Tony Franklin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Franklin_(kicker))___ 's 36-yard field goal 1:19 into the first quarter after three incomplete passes by quarterback ___E:Tony Eason U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Eason)___ (during the first of those three, tight end ___E:Lin Dawson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lin_Dawson)___ went down with torn ligaments in his knee). "I looked up at the message board", said Chicago linebacker ___E:Mike Singletary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Singletary)___ , "and it said that 15 of the 19 teams that scored first won the game. I thought, yeah, but none of those 15 had ever played the Bears."  Chicago struck back with a 7-play, 59-yard drive, featuring a 43-yard pass completion from McMahon to wide receiver ___E:Willie Gault U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Gault)___ , to set up kicker ___E:Kevin Butler U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Butler_(American_football))___ 's 28-yard field goal, tying the score at 3–3.

After both teams traded punts, defensive end ___E:Richard Dent U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Dent)___ and defensive tackle ___E:Steve McMichael U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_McMichael)___ forced a fumble on Eason that was recovered by defensive tackle ___E:Dan Hampton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Hampton)___ on the New England 13-yard line. Chicago then drove to the 3-yard line, but had to settle for a 24-yard field goal by Butler after defensive tackle ___E:William "The Refrigerator" Perry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Perry_(American_football))___ was tackled for a 1-yard loss while trying to throw his first NFL pass on a ___E:halfback option play U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halfback_option_play)___ .
The score gave Chicago their first lead of the game, 6–3, and they would never trail New England again.

On the Patriots' ensuing drive, Dent forced a fumble on running back ___E:Craig James U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craig_James_(running_back))___ , which was recovered by Singletary at the 13-yard line. Two plays later, Bears fullback ___E:Matt Suhey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Suhey)___ scored on an 11-yard touchdown run to increase the lead to 13–3.
New England took the ensuing kickoff and ran one play before the first quarter ended, which resulted in positive yardage for the first time in the game (a 3-yard run by James).
James, who earlier gained 258 total rushing yards in the three AFC playoff games, only managed to gain one yard on five rushing attempts in the Super Bowl.

After an incomplete pass and a tackle for a 4-yard loss by Hampton on tight end ___E:Greg Hawthorne U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Hawthorne)___ , the Patriots had to send in punter ___E:Rich Camarillo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rich_Camarillo)___ again, and wide receiver ___E:Keith Ortego U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Ortego)___ returned the ball 12 yards to the 41-yard line. The Bears subsequently drove 59 yards in 10 plays, featuring a 24-yard reception by Suhey, to score on McMahon's 2-yard touchdown run to increase their lead, 20–3. After the ensuing kickoff, New England lost 13 yards in 3 plays and had to punt again, but got the ball back with great field position when linebacker ___E:Don Blackmon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Blackmon)___ stripped the ball from Suhey and cornerback ___E:Raymond Clayborn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_Clayborn)___ recovered the fumble at the New England 46. During the punt, Ortego forgot what the play call was for the punt return, and the ensuing chaos resulted in him being penalized for handing off a ___E:fair catch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fair_catch)___ to cornerback ___E:Leslie Frazier U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leslie_Frazier)___ , who then suffered a career-ending knee injury while being tackled by Hawthorne.

Patriots head coach ___E:Raymond Berry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_Berry)___ then replaced Eason with ___E:Steve Grogan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Grogan)___ , who had spent the previous week hoping he would have the opportunity to step onto the NFL's biggest stage. "I probably won't get a chance", he had told reporters a few days before the game. "I just hope I can figure out some way to get on the field.

I could come in on the punt-block team and stand behind the line and wave my arms, or something."  But on his first drive, Grogan could only lead the Patriots to the Chicago 37-yard line, and they decided to punt rather than risk a long field goal attempt.

The Bears then marched 72 yards in 11 plays, which included a 29-yard reception by wide receiver ___E:Ken Margerum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Margerum)___ , moving the ball inside the Patriots' 10-yard line. New England kept Chicago out of the end zone, but Butler kicked a 24-yard field goal on the last play of the half to give the Bears a 23–3 halftime lead.
The end of the first half was controversial.
With 21 seconds left, McMahon scrambled to the Patriots' 3-yard line and was stopped inbounds.

With the clock ticking down, players from both teams were fighting, and the Bears were forced to snap the ball before the officials formally put it back into play, allowing McMahon to throw the ball out of bounds and stop the clock with three seconds left. The Bears were penalized five yards for delay of game, but according to NFL rules, 10 seconds should have also been run off the clock during such a deliberate clock-stopping attempt in the final two minutes of a half. In addition, a flag should have been thrown for fighting (also according to NFL rules).
This would have likely resulted in offsetting penalties, which would still allow for a field goal attempt.

Meanwhile, the non-call on the illegal snap was promptly acknowledged by the officials and reported by NBC sportscasters during halftime, but the resulting field goal was not taken away from the Bears (because of this instance, the NFL instructed officials to strictly enforce the 10-second run-off rule at the start of the 1986 season). [citation needed]

The Bears had dominated New England in the first half, holding them to 21 offensive plays (only four of which resulted in positive yardage), −19 total offensive yards, two pass completions, one first down, and 3 points.

While Eason was in the game, the totals were six possessions, one play of positive yardage out of 15 plays, no first downs, 3 points, 3 punts, 2 turnovers, no pass completions, and -36 yards of total offense.
Meanwhile, Chicago gained 236 yards and scored 23 points themselves.

After the Patriots received the second-half kickoff, they managed to get one first down, but then had to punt after Grogan was sacked twice, first by Dent for 5 yards, then by linebacker ___E:Otis Wilson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otis_Wilson)___ for 10. Camarillo, who punted four times in the first half, managed to pin the Bears back at their own 4-yard line with a then-Super Bowl record 62-yard punt. But the Patriots' defense still could not stop the Bears' offense.

On the first play, McMahon faked a handoff to Payton, then threw a 60-yard completion to Gault from his own end zone, followed by a 19-yard pass to tight end ___E:Emery Moorehead U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emery_Moorehead)___ .

Seven plays later, McMahon finished the Super Bowl-record 96-yard drive with a 1-yard touchdown run to increase Chicago's lead to 30–3. On the third play of the Patriots' second drive of the quarter, Grogan threw a pass that was tipped by tight end ___E:Derrick Ramsey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derrick_Ramsey)___ and intercepted by Bears cornerback ___E:Reggie Phillips U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggie_Phillips)___ (who filled in for Frazier), who returned it 28 yards for a touchdown to increase the lead to 37–3.

On the second play of their ensuing possession, the Patriots turned the ball over yet again when wide receiver ___E:Cedric Jones U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cedric_Jones_(wide_receiver))___ lost a fumble after catching a 19-yard pass from Grogan and taking a hit by safety ___E:Gary Fencik U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Fencik)___ , and linebacker ___E:Wilber Marshall U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilber_Marshall)___ returned the fumble 13 yards to New England's 37-yard line. Five plays later, McMahon's 27-yard pass to wide receiver ___E:Dennis Gentry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dennis_Gentry)___ moved the ball to the 1-yard line, setting up perhaps the most memorable moment of the game. Perry lined up as the running back in a power-I formation and scored on a 1-yard touchdown run, as he had done twice in the regular season.
His touchdown (while plowing over McGrew in the process) made the score 44–3 in favor of Chicago.
The Bears' three touchdowns is still a Super Bowl third quarter record for most points scored, while their 41-point lead is the record for largest margin going into the fourth quarter.

Perry's unexpected touchdown cost Las Vegas ___E:sports books U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_book)___ hundreds of thousands of dollars in losses from ___E:prop bets U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prop_bet)___ .

The Patriots finally reached the end zone early in the fourth quarter, advancing the ball 76 yards in 12 plays and scoring on an 8-yard fourth-down touchdown pass from Grogan to wide receiver ___E:Irving Fryar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irving_Fryar)___ .

The Bears' defense dominated the Patriots for the rest of the game, and recorded a forced fumble by defensive back ___E:Shaun Gayle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaun_Gayle)___ on Ramsey that was recovered by Singletary, followed by a 46-yard interception return to the New England 5-yard line by linebacker ___E:Jim Morrissey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Morrissey_(American_football))___ .

The Bears then turned the ball over on downs, but nevertheless capitalized on Morrissey's interception when defensive lineman ___E:Henry Waechter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Waechter)___ tackled Grogan in the end zone for a ___E:safety U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safety_(American_football_score))___ to make the final score 46–10.  After both teams exchanged punts, Chicago reached midfield to run out the clock and claim their first Super Bowl title.

One oddity in the Bears' victory was that Payton had a relatively poor performance running the football and did not score a touchdown in Super Bowl XX, his only Super Bowl appearance during his Hall of Fame career.
Many people including Mike Ditka have claimed that the reason for this was due to the fact that the Patriots' defensive scheme was centered on stopping Payton.
Although Payton was ultimately the Bears' leading rusher during the game, the Patriots' defense held him to only 61 yards on 22 carries, with his longest run being only 7 yards.

He was given several opportunities to score near the goal line, but New England stopped him every time before he reached the end zone (such as his 2-yard loss from the New England 3-yard line a few plays before Butler's second field goal, and his 2-yard run from the 4-yard line right before McMahon's first rushing touchdown).
Thus, Ditka opted to go for other plays to counter the Patriots' defense.
Ditka has since stated that his biggest regret of his career was not creating a scoring opportunity for Payton during the game.

McMahon, who completed 12 out of 20 passes for 256 yards, became the first quarterback to score two rushing touchdowns in the Super Bowl.  Gault finished the game with 129 receiving yards on just 4 receptions, an average of 32.3 yards per catch.
He also gained 49 yards on four kickoff returns.
The Patriots had the opening kickoff, two on scores and the last a free kick following the safety.
Suhey had 11 carries for 52 yards rushing and a touchdown, and caught a pass for 24 yards.
Singletary tied a Super Bowl record with 2 fumble recoveries.
Eason became the first Super Bowl starting quarterback without a pass completion,  finishing 0 for 6 with no interceptions.
Grogan completed 17 out of 30 passes for 177 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions.

Although fullback ___E:Tony Collins U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Collins_(American_football))___ was the Patriots' leading rusher, he was limited to just 4 yards on 3 carries, and caught 2 passes for 19 yards.
New England receiver wide ___E:Stephen Starring U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Starring)___ returned 7 kickoffs for 153 yards and caught 2 passes for 39 yards.
The Patriots, as a team, only recorded 123 total offensive yards, the second-lowest total in Super Bowl history.
